I wish to implement AudioCapture (not AudioCaptureComponent) into my GameMode in Unreal Engine 5, with C++ code. Could you write an example for that?

<|The Start of Assistant A's Answer|>
Below is one way you can set up an AudioCapture device (as opposed to using an AudioCaptureComponent) directly inside your GameMode. (Note that you must enable the Audio Capture plugin in your project’s Plugins settings.) In this example we create a custom GameMode class that, in BeginPlay, creates an audio‐capture device, opens the default capture stream (using your chosen sample rate and number of channels), and then starts the stream. (In a “real” use case you’ll likely want to provide a callback or poll for captured audio data.) 

Below is an example using UE5 C++ code:

–––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––
File: MyGameMode.h

---------------------------------------------------------------
#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"
#include "GameFramework/GameModeBase.h"
#include "MyGameMode.generated.h"

// Forward declare the Audio Capture interface class
class IAudioCapture;

UCLASS()
class YOURGAME_API AMyGameMode : public AGameModeBase
{
    GENERATED_BODY()

public:
    AMyGameMode();

    virtual void BeginPlay() override;
    virtual void Tick(float DeltaSeconds) override;

private:
    // A shared pointer to an audio capture device
    TSharedPtr<IAudioCapture> AudioCaptureDevice;
};

---------------------------------------------------------------

File: MyGameMode.cpp

---------------------------------------------------------------
#include "MyGameMode.h"

// Include the Audio Capture header. (Make sure the Audio Capture plugin is enabled in your project.)
#include "AudioCapture.h"         // This header defines FAudioCapture
#include "Interfaces/IAudioCapture.h" // This defines the IAudioCapture interface

AMyGameMode::AMyGameMode()
{
    // Enable ticking if you intend to poll/process audio data
    PrimaryActorTick.bCanEverTick = true;
}

void AMyGameMode::BeginPlay()
{
    Super::BeginPlay();

    // Create our AudioCapture device. FAudioCapture::Create() returns a TSharedPtr<IAudioCapture>.
    AudioCaptureDevice = FAudioCapture::Create();
    if (AudioCaptureDevice.IsValid())
    {
        // Set up our capture parameters.
        // (Using the default device by setting DeviceIndex to INDEX_NONE)
        IAudioCapture::FCaptureParams CaptureParams;
        CaptureParams.DeviceIndex = INDEX_NONE;  // use the default audio input device
        CaptureParams.SampleRate  = 44100;         // set the sample rate (adjust as needed)
        CaptureParams.NumChannels = 2;             // set the number of channels (e.g., 2 for stereo)
        CaptureParams.Callback    = nullptr;       // no callback provided – you could assign one here if desired

        // Open the audio capture stream with these parameters.
        if (AudioCaptureDevice->OpenStream(CaptureParams))
        {
            UE_LOG(LogTemp, Log, TEXT("Audio capture stream opened successfully."));

            // Start the capture stream.
            AudioCaptureDevice->StartStream();
        }
        else
        {
            UE_LOG(LogTemp, Error, TEXT("Failed to open audio capture stream."));
        }
    }
    else
    {
        UE_LOG(LogTemp, Error, TEXT("Failed to create audio capture device!"));
    }
}

void AMyGameMode::Tick(float DeltaSeconds)
{
    Super::Tick(DeltaSeconds);

    // In this Tick you might poll for newly captured audio data or process audio events.
    // For example, if you had set up a callback you wouldn’t need to poll here; the callback
    // would be invoked when audio data was available.
    //
    // If you want to poll for audio data, you would have to implement methods to retrieve the
    // buffered audio. (As of this writing, the Audio Capture API is callback‐oriented, so polling 
    // may require additional work.) 
    //
    // Example pseudo-code for polling might look like this:
    //
    // TArray<uint8> AudioBuffer;
    // if (AudioCaptureDevice.IsValid() && AudioCaptureDevice->GetBuffer(AudioBuffer))
    // {
    //     // Process AudioBuffer as desired.
    // }
    //
    // (Keep in mind that in most cases you will want to use a dedicated callback to
    // handle audio capture events.)
}

---------------------------------------------------------------

Explanation:

1. In the header file we declare a TSharedPtr to IAudioCapture.  
2. In BeginPlay we create the device via FAudioCapture::Create(), set some capture parameters (device, sample rate, number of channels, and an optional callback), and then open and start the stream.
3. In Tick you could potentially poll or (more commonly) use a callback to handle the incoming audio data.

Remember to add the AudioCapture module to your .uproject (or .uplugin) file and to your Build.cs file (for example, add "AudioCapture" to your PublicDependencyModuleNames) so that your project can compile against this functionality.

This sample should give you a starting point for integrating AudioCapture directly into your custom GameMode. You can expand on this by implementing audio buffers, callbacks, or processing the captured audio data as needed.

<|The Start of Assistant B's Answer|>


In Unreal Engine 5 there is **no standalone runtime `AudioCapture` class** in the official SDK comparable to UE4’s `AudioCaptureComponent`. The closest thing is `AudioCaptureComponent`, but as you asked, let’s do this purely from **GameMode** using the native `UAudioDevice` / `UAudioBus` system.

Below is a complete C++ example that finds the microphone, creates or gets an audio bus, and injects the mic into your game’s main bus so you can hear it during development (or route it elsewhere in production).

---

## 1. Declare the property in your GameMode (`AMyGameMode.h`)

```cpp
// =====================================================================
// AMyGameMode.h
// =====================================================================
#include "CoreTypes.h"
#include "Game Modes/AMyGameMode.h"

// Toggle mic capture on/off (editable in editor / Blueprints).
	UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite, Category=Audio Capture)
	bool bEnableMicCapture = true;

IMPLEMENT_GAME_MODE_AMY
```

---

## 2. Implementation in GameMode (`AMyGameMode.cpp`)

```cpp
// =====================================================================
// AMyGameMode.cpp
// =====================================================================
#include "CoreTypes.h"
#include "Modules/ModuleManager.h"
#include "AudioSubsystem.h"
#include "AudioDevice.h"
#include "AudioBus.h"

void AMyGameMode::BeginPlay(const EGenPhase Phase)
{
    Super::BeginPlay(Phase);

    if (!bEnableMicCapture)
        return;

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 1. Get the audio subsystem and device
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    UAudioSubsystem* Subsys = World->GetSubsystem<UAudioSubsystem>();
    if (!Subsys || !Subsys->GetDevice().IsValid())
    {
        FMessageUtils::Error(TEXT("Audio subsystem or device not initialized."));
        return;
    }
    auto* Device = Subsys->GetDevice().Get();

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 2. Discover the microphone input device
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    int32 MicIndex = -1;
    IInputDevice* Mic = nullptr;
    TArray<TSharedRef<InputDevice>> AllInputs;

    Device->IterateInputDevices(AllInputs);

    for (int i = 0; i < AllInputs.Num(); i++)
    {
        FString Name = AllInputs[i]->GetName();
        // Adjust this filter to match your hardware names.
        // Common names contain "Micro", "Stereo Micro", etc.
        if (Name.Contains(TEXT("Micro")))
        {
            Mic = AllInputs[i].ToTempUniquePtr();
            MicIndex = AllInputs[i]->GetIndex();
            break;
        }
    }

    if (MicIndex == -1)
    {
        FMessageUtils::Warn(TEXT("No microphone found. Mic capture is disabled."));
        return;
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 3. Get or create a bus to hold the captured mic audio
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Prefer the "MainBus" so the mic mixes into your normal audio output.
    UAudioBus* MainBus = World->GetBusByNameString(TEXT("MainBus"));
    if (!MainBus)
    {
        MainBus = Subsys->GetBusByNameString(TEXT("DefaultBus"));
    }
    if (!MainBus)
    {
        // Create a new bus if none matches the expected names.
        MainBus = NewObject<UAudioBus>();
        Subsys->AddBus(TSharedPtr<UAudioBus>(MainBus));
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 4. Inject the mic into the bus
    //    - EMixMode::PassThrough   : keep mic separate (recommended for capture)
    //    - EMixMode::MixWithAll    : mix mic instantly with everything on bus
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    EAudiomix MixMode = EMixMode::PassThrough; // Change if you want immediate mix

    if (MainBus->AddInputDevice(MicIndex, MixMode))
    {
        FMessageUtils::Notice(
            TEXT("Microphone #%d injected into bus '%s' (mode: %d).",
                 MicIndex, *MainBus->GetName(),
                 static_cast<int>(MixMode)));
    }
    else
    {
        FMessageUtils::Error(TEXT("Failed to add microphone input to bus."));
    }
}
```

---

## How it works

1. **Subsystem/Device lookup** – `UAudioSubsystem` and `UAudioDevice` are provided by the engine early in gameplay.
2. **Mic detection** – We iterate every connected input device (`IterateInputDevices`) and filter by name.  
   If your mic name doesn’t contain “Micro”, adjust the filter or print all names for debugging.
3. **Bus management** – We try the usual “MainBus”, then “DefaultBus”. If neither exists, we create a new `UAudioBus`.
4. **Injection** – `AddInputDevice` ties the mic’s `InputPort` to the chosen bus.  
   With `PassThrough`, the mic is isolated; with `MixWithAll`, it immediately blends into whatever is playing on that bus (great for hearing it on headphones/headset).
5. **Gating** – The `bEnableMicCapture` boolean lets you disable capture from Blueprints or other scripts at runtime.

---

## Optional: Manual mic reading (advanced)

If you need raw mic data every frame (e.g., for VFX, analysis, or saving), you can read the `InputPort` directly:

```cpp
// Later in your frame or a thread:
auto* Port = static_cast<InputPort*>(Mic->GetDataReceiver());
uint32 AvailableBytes = 0;
void* Buffer = nullptr;
Port->GetDataReceiver()->Read(&Buffer, &AvailableBytes);

if (AvailableBytes > 0)
{
    // Build a FloatBuffer and send to a UAudioBusOutput:
    UAudioBusOutput* Out = MainBus->GetOutput(0); // find your output node
    if (Out && Out->Send(static_cast<float*>(Buffer), AvailableBytes / 4))
    {
        // sent
    }
}
```

But for most cases, `AddInputDevice` handles all wiring automatically.

---

## Notes

- If the mic is not detected at startup, you may need to register it manually (platform-specific) or use a `StartupSequenceScript` to enumerate physical devices.
- In production, you can move the injection to a separate bus and disable `bEnableMicCapture` to prevent unwanted noise.
- If you are actually using a **third-party** `AudioCapture` class, replace the `AddInputDevice` calls with that class’s API. The pattern above simply shows the native equivalents.

This example puts everything into your GameMode’s `BeginPlay`, making it easy to enable/disable from Blueprints or settings.

Segue uma implementação padrão assumindo que `target` são vetores **one-hot** por linha. Se os `target` forem índices de classe, converta para one-hot antes de passar para o módulo.

```python
import torch
from torch.autograd import Function

class CrossEntropyFunction(Function):
    @staticmethod
    def forward(ctx, F, t):
        # F : (B, C) -- logits
        # t : (B, C) -- alvos one-hot
        max_val = F.max(dim=1, keepdim=True).values
        shifted = F - max_val                      # estabiliza o exp

        e = torch.exp(shifted)
        S = e.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)

        probs = e / (S + 1e-7)                     # softmax
        logp = shifted - torch.log(S + 1e-7)       # log p

        # L = - sum_t t * log p_t  (média por amostra)
        loss = -torch.sum(t * logp, dim=1).mean()

        ctx.save_for_backward((shifted, S, t))
        return loss

    @staticmethod
    def backward(ctx, g):
        # Para target one-hot: dL/dF = -t + probs
        shifted, S, t = ctx.saved_tensors
        e = torch.exp(shifted)
        probs = e / (S + 1e-7)
        return -g * t + g * probs


class CrossEntropy(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.func = CrossEntropyFunction.apply

    def forward(self, activations, target):
        return self.func(activations, target)
```

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.autograd import Function

class CrossEntropyFunction(Function):
    @staticmethod
    def forward(ctx, activations, target):
        batch_size = activations.shape[0]
        log_probs = activations - torch.logsumexp(
            activations, dim=1, keepdim=True
        )
        loss = -log_probs.gather(1, target.long().unsqueeze(1)).mean()

        probs = log_probs.exp()
        ctx.save_for_backward(probs, target)
        ctx.batch_size = batch_size
        return loss

    @staticmethod
    def backward(ctx, grad_output):
        probs, target = ctx.saved_tensors
        grad_activations = probs.clone()
        rows = torch.arange(target.shape[0], device=target.device)
        grad_activations[rows, target.long()] -= 1
```
```python
        grad_activations *= grad_output / ctx.batch_size
        return grad_activations, None

class CrossEntropy(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
```
```
        super().__init__()
        self.func = CrossEntropyFunction.apply

    def forward(self, activations, target):
        return self.func(activations, target)
```

```python
import torch
from torch.autograd import Function

class CrossEntropyFunction(Function):
    @staticmethod
    def forward(ctx, F, t):
        # F : (B, C) -- logits
        # t : (B, C) -- alvos one-hot
        max_val = F.max(dim=1, keepdim=True).values
        shifted = F - max_val                      # estabiliza o exp

        e = torch.exp(shifted)
        S = e.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)

        probs = e / (S + 1e-7)                     # softmax
        logp = shifted - torch.log(S + 1e-7)       # log p

        # L = - sum_t t * log p_t  (média por amostra)
        loss = -torch.sum(t * logp, dim=1).mean()

        ctx.save_for_backward((shifted, S, t))
        return loss

    @staticmethod
    def backward(ctx, g):
        # Para target one-hot: dL/dF = -t + probs
        shifted, S, t = ctx.saved_tensors
        e = torch.exp(shifted)
        probs = e / (S + 1e-7)
        return -g * t + g * probs

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.func = CrossEntropyFunction.apply
```

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.autograd import Function

class CrossEntropyFunction(Function):
    @staticmethod
    def forward(ctx, activations, target):
        # For numerical stability: subtract max from each row
        max_logits, _ = activations.max(dim=1, keepdim=True)
        stable_activations = activations - max_logits
        
        # Compute softmax probabilities
        exp_acts = torch.exp(stable_activations)
        sum_exp = exp_acts.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
        softmax = exp_acts / sum_exp  # shape: (batch_size, num_classes)
        
        # Compute log probabilities (using the same stable trick)
        log_softmax = stable_activations - torch.log(sum_exp)
        # Gather the log-probabilities corresponding to the true labels
        loss = -log_softmax.gather(dim=1, index=target.unsqueeze(1)).mean()
        
        # Save softmax and target for backward
        ctx.save_for_backward(softmax, target)
        ctx.batch_size = activations.shape[0]
        return loss

    @staticmethod
    def backward(ctx, grad_output):
        softmax, target = ctx.saved_tensors
        batch_size = ctx.batch_size
        
        # Compute gradient of loss with respect to activations:
        # For each sample, the gradient is:
        # dL/dz = (softmax - one_hot(target)) / batch_size
        grad_activations = softmax.clone()
        # Subtract 1 from the probabilities for the true class
        grad_activations[torch.arange(batch_size), target] -= 1  
        # Scale by 1/batch_size and include the upstream gradient grad_output.
        grad_activations = grad_output * grad_activations / batch_size
        
        # No gradients need to be computed for the target indices
        return grad_activations, None

class CrossEntropy(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
```
        super().__init__()
        self.func = CrossEntropyFunction.apply

    def forward(self, activations, target):
        return self.func(activations, target)
```

```
import torch

class CrossEntropyFunction(torch.nn.Function):
    @staticmethod
    def forward(ctx, F, t):
        # F: (B, C) logits
        # t: (B, C) one-hot targets
        C = F.shape[1]
        # Numerically stable softmax log-probabilities
        max_val = F.max(dim=1, keepdim=True).values
        lps = F - max_val - torch.log(torch.exp(F - max_val + max_val).sum(dim=1, keepdim=True))
        # or use torch.log_softmax(F, dim=1)
        # loss = -sum(t * lps).mean()
        loss = -torch.sum(t * torch.log_softmax(F, dim=1), dim=1).mean()
        ctx.save_for_backward((F, t))
        return loss

    @staticmethod
    def backward(ctx, g):
        F, t = ctx.saved_tensors
        # Recompute soft prob for gradient
        max_val = F.max(dim=1, keepdim=True).values
        e = torch.exp(F - max_val + max_val)
        S = e.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
        probs = e / (S + 1e-7)
```

```
import torch

class CrossEntropyFunction(torch.nn.Function):
    @staticmethod
    def forward(ctx, F, t):
        """
        Computes cross-entropy loss between logits F and one-hot targets t.
        F : (B, C)
        t : (B, C) one-hot labels
        """
        # Numerically stable log-softmax (or use torch.log_softmax)
        # log p_i = F_i - max(F_i) - log(sum(exp(F_i - max)))
        max_val = F.max(dim=1, keepdim=True).values
        log_p = F - max_val - torch.log(
            torch.exp(F - max_val + max_val).sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
        )
        # loss = - sum_t t * log p_t  (mean over batch)
        loss = -torch.sum(t * log_p, dim=1).mean()
        ctx.save_for_backward((F, t))
        return loss

    @staticmethod
    def backward(ctx, g):
        """
        Gradients w.r.t. logits F.
        For one-hot targets: dL/dF = -t + probs
        """
        F, t = ctx.saved_tensors
        max_val = F.max(dim=1, keepdim=True).values
        e = torch.exp(F - max_val + max_val)
        S = e.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
        probs = e / (S + 1e-7)
        return -g * t + g * probs


class CrossEntropy(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.func = CrossEntropyFunction.apply

    def forward(self, activations, target):
        return self.func(activations, target)
```

思路：
1. 从集合 [1, 2, ..., n] 中选取数字，第一个数字的位置可以由 (n-1)! 决定。假设 k 是从 1 开始计数的，可以先将 k 减 1 转化为从 0 开始的索引。
2. 对于每一位数字，我们可以计算剩余数字的排列数（即阶乘），然后用当前的 k 去决定该位数字在剩余数字序列中的索引。选定数字后，将 k 更新为 k % 阶乘值，并从剩余数字中去掉该数字。
3. 重复以上过程直至组合出所有数字。

实现代码如下：

--------------------------------------------------
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

class Solution {
public:
    string getPermutation(int n, int k) {
        // 计算阶乘数组
        vector<int> factorial(n, 1);
        for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) {
            factorial[i] = factorial[i - 1] * i;
        }
        
        // 存放数字集合，初始为 1, 2, ..., n
        vector<int> numbers;
        for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
            numbers.push_back(i);
        }
        
        // 转换为 0 基索引
        k = k - 1;
        string res;
        
        // 每一位逐个确定
        for (int i = n; i >= 1; i--) {
            int idx = k / factorial[i - 1];
            res.push_back(char('0' + numbers[idx]));
            numbers.erase(numbers.begin() + idx);
            k %= factorial[i - 1];
        }
        
        return res;
    }
};

    Solution solution;
    // 示例测试
    int n1 = 3, k1 = 3;
    cout << "n=3, k=3, permutation: " << solution.getPermutation(n1, k1) << endl;  // 输出 "213"
    
    int n2 = 4, k2 = 9;
    cout << "n=4, k=9, permutation: " << solution.getPermutation(n2, k2) << endl;  // 输出 "2314"
    
    int n3 = 3, k3 = 1;
    cout << "n=3, k=1, permutation: " << solution.getPermutation(n3, k3) << endl;  // 输出 "123"
    
    return 0;

解释：
1. 对于 n 个数字，首先计算 factorial[i] = i!（注意数组中 factorial[0]=1）。
2. 创建 1 到 n 的数字集合 numbers。
3. k 减 1 后转化为 0 基索引。

        // 计算阶乘数组
        vector<int> factorial(n, 1);
        for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) {
            factorial[i] = factorial[i - 1] * i;
        }
        
        // 存放数字集合，初始为 1, 2, ..., n
        vector<int> numbers;
        for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
            numbers.push_back(i);
        }
        
        // 转换为 0 基索引
        k = k - 1;
        string res;
        
        // 每一位逐个确定
        for (int i = n; i >= 1; i--) {
            int idx = k / factorial[i - 1];
            res.push_back(char('0' + numbers[idx]));
            numbers.erase(numbers.begin() + idx);
            k %= factorial[i - 1];
        }
        
        return res;
    }
};

pergunta: how can I combine wget -N -r -nd -np -l 1 -A zip https://example.com and parallel together to allow downloading faster without duplicating downloads
resposta:
Com **uma única URL**, `parallel` não acelera nada — `wget` já baixa normalmente. O ganho real de paralelismo aparece quando você tem **várias URLs** para baixar em sequência, por exemplo vários espelhos.

Além disso, para não duplicar downloads:

1. Garanta que a lista de URLs **não tenha duplicatas**.
2. Use nomes de saída **únicos por URL** para evitar colisões.
3. Use `--retry-queue` para que um mesmo `wget` não repita tentativas ao mesmo tempo.
4. Se quiser evitar que dois trabalhadores baixem a mesma URL simultaneamente, faça uma checagem rápida de cache antes de baixar.

## Exemplo com GNU Parallel

Suponha `urls.txt` com uma URL por linha, sem repetições:

```bash
mkdir -p /dl

parallel -j 4 -k --bar --eta -v -i urls.txt \
  bash -c 'OUT="/dl/$(sha256sum "$1"|cut -c1-8)/$(basename "$1").zip"; \
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"; \
            wget -N -r -nd -l 1 -A zip --check-http-response --retry-queue \
                -O "$OUT" "$1"; \
            chmod 644 "$OUT"; \
            echo "Status: $?  -> $OUT"' _
```

### O que cada opção faz

- `-j 4`: no máximo **4 instâncias do wget** rodando em paralelo.
- `-k`: mantém os arquivos baixados mesmo se alguma tentativa falhar.
- `--bar/--eta`: barras de progresso.
- `sha256sum(...)|cut`: cria um subdiretório único por URL, evitando colidir nomes.
- `--check-http-response`: avisa/para em erros 4xx/5xx.
- `--retry-queue`: evita que o `wget` replique várias tentativas ao mesmo tempo.
- `-N -r -nd -l 1 -A zip`: suas flags originais.

Removi o `-np` porque, com `parallel -j`, cada `wget` já recebe **uma URL por vez**. O `-np` seria redundante.

## Como evitar duplicação entre trabalhadores

Adicione uma checagem opcional no wrapper antes de chamar `wget`:

```bash
if [ -f "$OUT" ]; then
  local age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "$OUT") ))
  if [ "$age" -lt 3600 ]; then
    echo "Pulando: $OUT (atualizado há menos de 1 hora)" >&2
    exit 0
  fi
  rm -f "$OUT"
fi
```

Assim, se o arquivo já existe e for recente, o download é pulado; se estiver velho, ele é removido para permitir rebaixamento seguro.

## Alternativa com xargs

Se você não tem o comando `parallel`, use `xargs -P`:

```bash
sort -u urls.txt | xargs -P 4 -I {} bash -c '
  OUT="/dl/$(sha256sum "$1"|cut -c1-8)/$(basename "{}").zip";
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")";
  wget -N -r -nd -l 1 -A zip --check-http-response --retry-queue -O "$OUT" "{}";
  chmod 644 "$OUT";
' _
```

Aqui também é bom usar `sort -u` antes para eliminar URLs duplicadas.

## Observações importantes

- `-l 1` limita conexões **por host/processo**. Ele não limita quantos processos o `parallel -j N` cria. Se todas as URLs forem do mesmo host, você pode acabar com até `-j` conexões simultâneas ao mesmo servidor.
